newsitem.title: ESTONIA: EBRD WANTS TO BOOST HOME OWNERSHIP.
newsitem.headline: EBRD WANTS TO BOOST HOME OWNERSHIP.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Monday it wants to boost home ownership in Estonia and expects to help banks introduce more sophisticated products targeted at the sector.

The bank, which has stakes in several leading Estonian banks, also said it was interested in the development of a mortgage finance agency, which will be one of the first in the former Communist states of eastern Europe.
"We would not...be lending standard credit lines to Estonian banks," Jonathan Harfield, EBRD representative to Estonia, Latvia, Hungary, Poland and Bulgaria, told Reuters.
"We are moving to more advanced and longer-term products: housing loans, subordinated debt, which are quite sophisticated products in any market," he added in an interview.
The EBRD has already taken a stake in Hoiupank , Maapank and the Estonian Investment Bank. It has given credit lines to leading bank Hansapank and Maapank.
Harfield said the EBRD was interested in the housing sector as there was no more tangible evidence of people's participation in the wealth of a nation than when they own their own homes.
"One project already underway is two housing loans in total worth 27 million marks to Hansapank and Hoiupank," he added.
"These loans are for people to purchase their principle private residences," he said.
The bank is also very interested in the establishment of a mortgage finanace agency in Estonia.
The agency is a cooperation project between the major banks in Estonia with Hansa Investments taking a leading, coordinating role, Harfield said.
The aim of the agency is to securitise bank mortgages and may one day lead to the creation of a secondary market for mortgages, such as already works in the U.S.
"The agency will give much greater access to long-term housing finance for the average individual," Harfield said.
"We will be a potenial equity investor in the mortage agency," he added.
